title: Optimizing Dynamic-Shape Neural Networks on Accelerators via On-the-Fly Micro-Kernel Polymerization
problem: Dynamic-shape neural networks have shapes determined at runtime, making static compilation expensive and impractical. Existing static-shape tensor compilers cannot efficiently handle the computational optimization challenges of dynamic scenarios.
motivation: Dynamic-shape neural networks are increasingly used in intelligent applications to address complex tasks, requiring efficient optimization for practical deployment on accelerators.
method: MikPoly is a two-stage dynamic-shape tensor compiler that pre-generates multiple static micro-kernels and dynamically combines them at runtime. It employs a lightweight cost model based on tensor operator shapes known at runtime to select the best micro-kernel combination for each dynamic shape encountered.
key_novelty: On-the-fly dynamic combination of statically compiled micro-kernels using runtime shape information and a lightweight cost model for efficient dynamic-shape tensor optimization.
contributions: MikPoly: A novel dynamic-shape tensor compiler based on micro-kernel polymerization
Two-stage optimization combining static micro-kernel generation with dynamic runtime selection
Lightweight cost model for shape-aware kernel selection at runtime
1.49× average performance improvement over vendor libraries on GPU and NPU accelerators
primary_theme: dynamic tensor compilation via runtime kernel selection
